---
title: "Checklist for Equitable Data Selection for Women's Healthcare"
---
The checklist is based on the translation of clinicians perceptions of women's health [@Heaney2025] into dataset requirements. The method is outlined in @Heaney2026.


Tick off each item as you go. Your progress is saved in your browser.

```{=html}
<div class="progress-wrap">
  <span id="progress-text">0 / 20 complete</span>
  <button id="reset-btn" type="button">Reset</button>
  <div class="progress-bar-outer"><div class="progress-bar-inner" id="progress-bar"></div></div>
</div>
```

<!--
  HOW TO EDIT: change the text inside .item-title (the big heading)
  and .item-desc (the explanation underneath). Don't remove the
  <input type="checkbox"> lines. Rename sections in the <h2> lines.
-->

::: {.checklist-section .lilac}
## Necessities

```{=html}
<label class="check-item"><input type="checkbox"><div><span class="item-title">Contain both male and female patients(if condition being studied affects both)</span><span class="item-desc">You may wish to compare women's data vs men's data, as they can have different symptoms, treatment options and difference in prevalence of condition</span></div></label>
<label class="check-item"><input type="checkbox"><div><span class="item-title">Contains a range of participant ages</span><span class="item-desc">Women can have different treatment plans/differential diagnosis based on their age.</span></div></label>
<label class="check-item"><input type="checkbox"><div><span class="item-title">	Is it a recent dataset or could recent advancements in the condition being studied limit how old the dataset can be</span><span class="item-desc">Women's health has progressed in the last number of years both in treatment options and knowledge of how symptoms present in women and men. Consider how old your dataset can be given recent advancements. This checklist was developed based on opinions of clinicians in 2023, there may be additional timerelated elements to consider.</span></div></label>
<label class="check-item"><input type="checkbox"><div><span class="item-title">Where was the data gathered</span><span class="item-desc">This checklist is based off European clinicians perspectives, there may be country and government specific elements to consider.</span></div></label>
```
:::

::: {.checklist-section .lilac}
## Sex Specific Factors

```{=html}
<label class="check-item"><input type="checkbox"><div><span class="item-title">Are women specific stages such as menstruation and menopause included</span><span class="item-desc">Menstruation and menopause can impact chronic diseases.Changes in menstruation can indicate underlying health conditions. Similarly 'menstuation conditions' such as Endometriosis, PCOS/PMOS can increase the likelihood chronic condtions such as heart disease and diabetes. </span></div></label>
<label class="check-item"><input type="checkbox"><div><span class="item-title">Is pregnancy status known</span><span class="item-desc">Pregnancy or plans to become pregnant can impact the type of medication women with chronic diseases can use.</span></div></label>
<label class="check-item"><input type="checkbox"><div><span class="item-title">Is history of pregnancy complications known</span><span class="item-desc">Events that happen during pregnancy such as 'preaclamsia' or 'gestational diabeties' can be indicators of a patients health in the future.</span></div></label>
<label class="check-item"><input type="checkbox"><div><span class="item-title">Does your dataset include transgendered patients</span><span class="item-desc">Be aware if there are trans patients in your dataset, e.g. trans men may still need gynacology services.</span></div></label>
<label class="check-item"><input type="checkbox"><div><span class="item-title">Are there conditions that affect more women/men present in the dataset</span><span class="item-desc">There are conditions that affect more women then men (and vice versa) this may impact the representation in your datases. Consider what an equitable split may look like</span></div></label>
```
:::

::: {.checklist-section .lilac}
## Clinician Information
```{=html}
<label class="check-item"><input type="checkbox"><div><span class="item-title">Is the sex of the clinician known?</span><span class="item-desc">The sex of the clinician may impact the care women recieve.</span></div></label>
<label class="check-item"><input type="checkbox"><div><span class="item-title">s the specialisation of the clinician know</span><span class="item-desc">The specialisation of the clinician may impact the type of treatment the patient has access to</span></div></label>
```
:::


::: {.checklist-section .lilac}
## Patient Specific Factors

```{=html}
<label class="check-item"><input type="checkbox"><div><span class="item-title">Is there a need to consider comorbidities</span><span class="item-desc">Comorbidities are more common in women and can impact treatment plans.</span></div></label>
<label class="check-item"><input type="checkbox"><div><span class="item-title">Are pain scales present/necessary</span><span class="item-desc">Women tend to report lower pain levels in comparison to men. Consider this if painscales are in your data and indeed if they are necessary for your model.</span></div></label>
<label class="check-item"><input type="checkbox"><div><span class="item-title">Is ethnicity known</span><span class="item-desc">Different ethnicities have different risk factors for various conditions.</span></div></label>
<label class="check-item"><input type="checkbox"><div><span class="item-title">Are cultural factors known</span><span class="item-desc">A womans culture may impact their wants/needs in medication and treatment plans, e.g. some cultures are not comfortable stoping periods completely or being on a form of birth control.This limits the options patient has..</span></div></label>
<label class="check-item"><input type="checkbox"><div><span class="item-title">Is the location known(of the patients home)</span><span class="item-desc">The patients loction impacts their access to services. Location can be a proxcy variable e.g. for socioeconomic status.</span></div></label>
<label class="check-item"><input type="checkbox"><div><span class="item-title">Are there personal patient factors e.g. carer responsibilities, history of abuse</span><span class="item-desc">Carer responsibilities and abuse can reduce a patients ability to be seen medically and therefor these patients may not be represented in your data. Models aiming to schedule patients appointments should be partularly mindful of this. Social pressures may impact the types of treatment a patient can access.</span></div></label>
<label class="check-item"><input type="checkbox"><div><span class="item-title">Are there treatment plans/medication known.</span><span class="item-desc">Treatment plans and medication can vary based on sex and gender.</span></div></label>
<label class="check-item"><input type="checkbox"><div><span class="item-title">Is the length of diagnosis known</span><span class="item-desc">Women on average take longer to get a diagnosis then men, be aware of this if you plan on considering diagnostic length. If your data was collected during a set time frame there may be women in your data who were diagnosed after the data collection period, or they may be removed since they didn't have the diagnosis yet.</span></div></label>
```
:::

::: {.checklist-section .lilac}
## Domain Knowledge - i.e. knowledge of the area being studied

```{=html}
<label class="check-item"><input type="checkbox"><div><span class="item-title">Is there known gender or sex differences in the studied condition(s)</span><span class="item-desc">There are conditions where women and men have different treatment options, different side effects to medication, different symptoms.</span></div></label>

<label class="check-item"><input type="checkbox"><div><span class="item-title">Is there additional resources to bridge the data science to medical science gap</span><span class="item-desc">Some datasets can be difficult to interpret, well documented datasets, domain experts who Work in the area are a great resource</span></div></label>
<label class="check-item"><input type="checkbox"><div><span class="item-title">Is there a lot of background knowledge needed to understand the data</span><span class="item-desc">Ensure all columns are understood and how they interact with each other.</span></div></label>
<label class="check-item"><input type="checkbox"><div><span class="item-title">Is there domain experts to call upon who know the data</span><span class="item-desc">A 'Domain expert' is anyone who knows the medical intricacys of the researched condition. They can help with unclear results and explain condition in dept for example: doctors, biomedical scientist, clinical nurse specialists</span></div></label>

```
:::


```{=html}
<script>
(function () {
  var boxes = document.querySelectorAll('.check-item input[type="checkbox"]');
  var bar = document.getElementById('progress-bar');
  var text = document.getElementById('progress-text');
  var KEY = 'dataset-checklist-v1';

  function load() {
    try { return JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY)) || {}; } catch (e) { return {}; }
  }
  function save(state) {
    try { localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(state)); } catch (e) {}
  }
  function update() {
    var done = 0, state = {};
    boxes.forEach(function (b, i) {
      if (b.checked) done++;
      state[i] = b.checked;
    });
    save(state);
    bar.style.width = (done / boxes.length * 100) + '%';
    text.textContent = done + ' / ' + boxes.length + ' complete';
  }

  var saved = load();
  boxes.forEach(function (b, i) {
    b.checked = !!saved[i];
    b.addEventListener('change', update);
  });
  document.getElementById('reset-btn').addEventListener('click', function () {
    boxes.forEach(function (b) { b.checked = false; });
    update();
  });
  update();
})();
</script>
```
